Interdisciplinary Data Analytics and X Double Major Programme

Interdisciplinary Data Analytics & X Double Major Programme

Applicable to students admitted in 2025-26

 

 

 

 

Major Programme Requirement

 

Students are required to complete a minimum of 90 units of courses. Students will take the Interdisciplinary Data Analytics offered by CUHK as the 1st major, and choose from one of the Majors offered by CUHK or CUHK(SZ) as specified in 3. below as their 2nd Major. Some courses offered by CUHK and CUHK(SZ) are equivalent/substitute. Please refer to the list of equivalent/substitute courses for details.

Explanatory Notes:

1.

Students enrolled in the Double Major Programme should normally spend four regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study, except otherwise specified in 2. and 3. below. It applies to all students, including those who select a 2nd Major offered by CUHK.

2.

Students may apply for the Co-operative Education (Co-op) Programme (5 units) in Year 2 or above. Students joining the Co-op Programme will undertake a full-time placement in two specific work terms, including one summer session and one regular term (i.e., term 1 or term 2). They have to spend at least three regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study.

3.

Students who join term-time exchange programme have to spend at least three regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study.

4.

Students enrolled in the Double Major programme can take equivalent/substitute courses either at CUHK or CUHK(SZ). The list of equivalent/substitute courses is available at this link (www.sci.cuhk.edu.hk/IDADM). Students should not take a course and its equivalent/substitute course. Should they do so, only one course will be counted towards the fulfilment of units requirements. Grades of relevant equivalent/substitute courses taken at CUHK(SZ) will be transferred to CUHK for the purpose of calculation of GPA, Major GPA and credit units.

5.

Students normally have to declare their 2nd Major by the end of their first year of study.

6.

All courses at 2000 and above level and courses labeled as # in the requirements of the 1st Major Programme, as well as 3 units of research component course offered by the 2nd Major, will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

7.

Courses taken to fulfil the requirements of the 1st Major cannot be counted towards the fulfilment of requirements of the 2nd Major, and vice versa.

8.

Under very special circumstances and subject to approval by the Major programmes concerned, students may opt out of the Double Major Programme and register for the 1st Major programme only, and they will be required to take an additional 3 units of research component course offered by the 2nd Major to fulfill the unit requirement of the 1st Major which is 60 units. The 3 units of research component will also be included in the calculation of Major GPA. The decision to opt out is irrevocable. Students who have been approved to opt out from the Double Major Programme should still observe the requirements in 1. above. If the students have not yet declared a 2nd Major at the time of opting out, they should fulfil the requirements of one of the areas under the 1st Major and take the additional 3 units of research component offered by the 2nd Major corresponding to the particular area.

9.

Students may be required to complete prerequisite courses for certain courses listed in the study scheme.

[a]

Non-JUPAS and JUPAS admittees without HKDSE Mathematics Extended Modules I or II may consider taking STAT1011 in advance for enriching statistics knowledge, if necessary.

[b]

For students who choose Integrated BBA programme as 2nd Major, they are required to take 15 units from Group A. Students will graduate with General Business Concentration and are not allowed to declare Minor in Business.

[a]

Students may apply to study in the Co-operative Education Programme (Co-op@CUHK) (5 units) in Year 2 or above. Students who study the Co-op programme will take COOP4001, which is a 1-unit course to be taken in each of the Summer Session of Year 3 and Term 1 of Year 4. They will undertake a full-time placement in two specific work terms, during which they are not allowed to register for any other courses except the 1-unit continuous assessment course COOP4001.

[b]

When students are studying at CUHK(SZ), they can take equivalent or substitute courses at CUHK(SZ) to fulfill the requirements of CUHK.

[c]

Students enrolled in different 2nd Major programmes may refer to the individual recommended course patterns developed by each programme, which may deviate slightly from the general recommended course pattern above.

[d]

The recommended course pattern of College GE courses varies according to student’s college affiliation.

[e]

Approval has been granted by the Registrar for students of the Interdisciplinary Data Analytics & X Double Major Programme to take 19 units of courses in Term 1 and/or Term 2 of Year 1.

[f]

If students have taken a 3-unit UGE course at CUHK(SZ), the 3 units will be transferred to CUHK. Currently all GE courses in CUHK(SZ) are 3-unit.

[a]

 

Students may apply to study in the Co-operative Education Programme (Co-op@CUHK) (5 units) in Year 2 or above. Students who study the Co-op programme will take COOP4001, which is a 1-unit course to be taken in each of the Summer Session of Year 3 and Term 1 of Year 4. They will undertake a full-time placement in two specific work terms, during which they are not allowed to register for any other courses except the 1-unit continuous assessment course COOP4001.

When students are studying at CUHK(SZ), they can take equivalent or substitute courses at CUHK(SZ) to fulfill the requirements of CUHK.

[e]

If students have taken a 3-unit UGE course at CUHK(SZ), the 3 units will be transferred to CUHK. Currently all GE courses in CUHK(SZ) are 3-unit.

Study Scheme
Learning Outcomes
 
Interdisciplinary Data Analytics and X Double Major Programme_Learning Outcomes

1. Major Programme:

 

Upon completion of the Programme, students will have:

Knowledge outcomes

Interdisciplinary knowledge

By completing the programme, graduates will have acquired knowledge of:

(1)      mathematics, statistics and business management;

(2)      computer-based information and data processing;

(3)      computational and statistical methods and tools.

Critical Thinking/Computational Thinking

By completing the programme, graduates will have developed the following abilities related to consciousness of data analytics:

(1)      consider problems from different perspectives;

(2)      identify and criticise the abuse and misuse of data analytics;

(3)      analyse quantitative evidence in a critical manner;

(4)      analyse and interpret large quantity of data.

 

Skills Outcomes

Generic Competencies

By completing the programme, graduates will demonstrate competency in:

(1)      integrating knowledge in engineering, science and business, and solving interdisciplinary problems;

(2)      communicating effectively in a scientific and business context;

(3)      working in teams;

(4)      programming and using information technology.

Professional Skills

By completing the programme, graduates will have acquired professional skills on:

(1)      formulating data analytical and related engineering, science and business problems;

(2)      analysing data accurately using mathematics, statistics, computer and other technologies;

(3)      communicating and conveying results of the analysis to both general public and professional practitioners;

(4)      generating and evaluating alternatives, developing practical solutions and proposing strategies in a global environment;

(5)      problem-solving in an inter-disciplinary context.

 

Attitude/Value Outcomes

By completing the programme, graduates will have acquired a positive attitude on:

(1)      awareness of importance of data analytics and data ethics in daily life;

(2)      appreciation of different aspects of knowledge in the era of Big Data;

(3)      commitment to contribute to the development of GBA.
